_comment: The whole promotion partition (10,000 seeds), one checkpoint, one seed per rollout.
The head 3,500 seeds were the census already published; the tail 6,500 are new, measured
to answer the rate question the fork artifact left open.
'cleared but not judged a win' = truncated at floor 17 in a generated act 2, which the
fork showed is the AdvanceAfterNode exit (see act2_boss_completion_fork_20260919.json).
20 of the 21 carry dead_end_reasons=empty_action_mask from the census row itself; the 21st
(130012038) predates that field and its reason was established separately by evaluate_policy.
Head and tail disagree about the size of the class (1/26 vs 20/60) and no explanation was
found, so both are reported; the pooled figure is quoted with that split visible.
Reproduction checks: 3,500 head seeds re-measured with the current code -- 0 category
disagreements and 0 step-count differences; 3 tail truncating seeds re-measured in a
sequential process -- all 3 still truncate at the same step counts.
established: over the full 10,000-seed promotion partition this checkpoint completes 68 floor-17 wins: 3 in generated act 1 and 65 in generated act 2
the same window contains 21 generated act-2 runs that cleared the act boss and were never judged a win, i.e. 24.4% [16.6,34.5] of the 86 act-2 boss kills
generated act 1 loses 245 of its 248 boss arrivals inside the fight and shows zero empty-mask endings, which is the asymmetry the two-exit code predicts

the three act-1 completions the tail found are exactly the ledger's named seeds for this checkpoint (130015189, 130017978, 130019400), so the census and the win ledger now agree seed by seed rather than only being 'not in conflict'
sharding does not change results: the census is reproducible across 1, 2, 4 and 5 concurrent processes
not_established: why the head window yields 1 mis-exit in 26 act-2 kills and the tail 20 in 60 -- determinism was checked in both directions, so this is reported as unexplained window heterogeneity, not pooled silently
whether the 21 runs would all have flipped under a different claim order; the per-run fork was replayed for one seed only
any rate for other arms or checkpoints -- this is one checkpoint on one partition
scope: simulator_act1 label over the act1 stage's promotion partition; mixed-act population split by generated act
